questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter_name: States of Matter and Phase Changes
questions.question_text: Which statement best matches kinetic particle theory?
questions.answer: Particles are in continuous motion

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter_name: States of Matter and Phase Changes
questions.question_text: During melting of a pure solid, supplied energy mainly helps to?
questions.answer: Overcome intermolecular attractions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter_name: States of Matter and Phase Changes
questions.question_text: Differentiate evaporation and boiling.
questions.answer: Evaporation occurs at the surface over a range of temperatures, while boiling occurs throughout a liquid at its boiling point when vapour pressure matches external pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter_name: States of Matter and Phase Changes
questions.question_text: Why can temperature remain constant during a phase change despite heating?
questions.answer: The supplied energy is used mainly to overcome intermolecular attractions rather than increase average kinetic energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter_name: States of Matter and Phase Changes
questions.question_text: Explain solid, liquid and gas behavior using particle arrangement, motion, attractions and response to heating.
questions.answer: Award marks for arrangement, particle motion, relative attractive forces, compressibility/shape differences, and effect of heating/phase change.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: One mole contains approximately how many particles?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The textbook uses approximately what molar gas volume at room temperature and pressure?
questions.answer: 24 dm³ mol⁻¹

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Why must a chemical equation be balanced before stoichiometric calculations?
questions.answer: Balanced coefficients provide the mole ratios required to relate amounts of reactants and products consistently with conservation of atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Define molar concentration.
questions.answer: Molar concentration is amount of solute in moles per unit volume of solution, commonly mol dm⁻³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Describe a reliable method for solving a mass-to-mass stoichiometry problem.
questions.answer: Award marks for balancing the equation, converting known mass to moles, using mole ratio, converting target moles to mass, and checking units/significant reasonableness.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Oxidation can be described as?
questions.answer: Loss of electrons

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In electrolysis, positive ions move toward the?
questions.answer: Cathode

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What is an oxidation state used for?
questions.answer: It is a bookkeeping number used to track electron distribution and identify oxidation/reduction changes in compounds and ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Differentiate a voltaic cell and an electrolytic cell.
questions.answer: A voltaic cell converts spontaneous chemical energy to electrical energy; an electrolytic cell uses electrical energy to drive a non-spontaneous chemical change.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Explain oxidation, reduction, electron transfer and electrode roles in a simple electrochemical process.
questions.answer: Award marks for oxidation as electron loss, reduction as gain, electron flow, anode/cathode roles, and relation to overall redox reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For a reaction to occur, colliding particles generally need?
questions.answer: Sufficient energy and suitable orientation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A catalyst increases reaction rate mainly by?
questions.answer: Providing a lower-activation-energy pathway

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: How can increasing temperature increase reaction rate?
questions.answer: Particles move faster, collide more frequently and a larger fraction of collisions have enough energy to overcome activation energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Why can powdered solid react faster than a large lump of the same mass?
questions.answer: Powdering increases exposed surface area, giving more available collision sites per unit time.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Explain how concentration, temperature, surface area and catalysts affect reaction rate using collision theory.
questions.answer: Award one mark for each factor and one mark for linking all effects to frequency/effectiveness of collisions or activation energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A salt is best described as?

options.text: An ionic compound containing cations and anions

questions.answer: An ionic compound containing cations and anions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which method is suitable for preparing a soluble salt from an acid and an insoluble base?

options.text: Add excess base, filter, then crystallize

questions.answer: Add excess base, filter, then crystallize

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Why is solubility information important when choosing a salt-preparation method?
questions.answer: It determines whether precipitation, neutralization with excess solid, or another separation/crystallization route is suitable.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What is the purpose of crystallization in salt preparation?
questions.answer: It separates purified solid crystals from a concentrated solution as solvent is removed or the solution cools.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Compare methods for preparing a soluble salt and an insoluble salt in the laboratory.
questions.answer: Award marks for choosing reactants, reaction/neutralization or precipitation, filtration where needed, concentration/crystallization for soluble salt, and washing/drying precipitate for insoluble salt.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric nitrogen into?
questions.answer: More reactive nitrogen compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Oxides of nitrogen can contribute to?
questions.answer: Photochemical smog and acid-forming pollution

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Why is nitrogen important to living organisms?
questions.answer: Nitrogen is needed to build amino acids/proteins, nucleic acids and other essential biological molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: State one environmental concern associated with sulphur dioxide.
questions.answer: It can contribute to acid deposition and respiratory/environmental harm when present as an air pollutant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Discuss useful roles and environmental impacts of important nitrogen and sulphur compounds.
questions.answer: Award marks for fertilizer/industrial uses, nitrogen biological importance, nitrogen-oxide pollution, sulphur compound uses, and sulphur-dioxide/acid-deposition concerns.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Anhydrous copper(II) sulfate can be used to test for?
questions.answer: Water

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Hard water commonly contains significant amounts of?
questions.answer: Calcium and magnesium ions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Why is water treated before public supply?
questions.answer: Treatment removes or reduces suspended matter, harmful microorganisms and undesirable contaminants so water is safer and more suitable for use.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: State one disadvantage and one possible advantage of hard water.
questions.answer: Disadvantage: scale/soap wastage. Possible advantage: calcium and magnesium ions can contribute useful dietary minerals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Explain sources of water contamination and major steps used to improve water quality for human use.
questions.answer: Award marks for contamination sources, sedimentation/filtration, disinfection, chemical/quality monitoring, and responsible pollution prevention.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Organic chemistry mainly studies compounds of?
questions.answer: Carbon

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A structural formula shows?

options.text: How atoms are connected in a molecule

questions.answer: How atoms are connected in a molecule

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What is a homologous series?
questions.answer: A family of organic compounds with the same functional group and general formula, similar chemical properties and a gradual change in physical properties.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What are structural isomers?
questions.answer: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements of atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Explain how functional groups, homologous series and structural formulae help organize organic chemistry.
questions.answer: Award marks for each concept, relation to chemical properties, general formula/patterns, and an original example.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A hydrocarbon contains only?
questions.answer: Carbon and hydrogen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Alkenes contain at least one?
questions.answer: Carbon-carbon double bond

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Differentiate saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons.
questions.answer: Saturated hydrocarbons contain only carbon-carbon single bonds; unsaturated hydrocarbons contain one or more carbon-carbon multiple bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Why can incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons be harmful?
questions.answer: It can produce carbon monoxide and soot, wasting fuel and causing serious health/air-quality hazards.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Compare alkanes and alkenes in bonding, general reactivity and one characteristic reaction.
questions.answer: Award marks for saturation difference, single vs double bond, relative reactivity, substitution for alkanes, and addition for alkenes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The functional group of an alcohol is?
questions.answer: –OH

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Fermentation can produce ethanol from?

options.text: Sugars using microorganisms such as yeast

questions.answer: Sugars using microorganisms such as yeast

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Why are lower alcohols often soluble in water?
questions.answer: Their hydroxyl group can form hydrogen bonds with water; solubility generally decreases as the hydrocarbon chain becomes larger.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What type of compound can ethanol form on oxidation under suitable conditions?
questions.answer: It can be oxidized toward an aldehyde and further to a carboxylic acid such as ethanoic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Describe preparation, important properties and selected reactions/uses of ethanol.
questions.answer: Award marks for fermentation or another valid preparation route, physical property, combustion, oxidation or other reaction, and a responsible industrial/use example.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The carboxylic-acid functional group is?
questions.answer: –COOH

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A carboxylic acid reacting with a carbonate typically produces salt, water and?
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Why do carboxylic acids show acidic behavior?
questions.answer: The carboxyl group can donate a proton in aqueous conditions, producing carboxylate ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What is formed when a carboxylic acid reacts with a suitable alcohol under esterification conditions?
questions.answer: An ester and water are formed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Explain reactions of carboxylic acids with metals, bases, carbonates and alcohols.
questions.answer: Award marks for correct product patterns for the first three acid reactions, ester formation with alcohol, and representative equations/naming without copying textbook examples.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Proteins are built from?
questions.answer: Amino acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Carbohydrates commonly serve as?

options.text: Important energy sources and structural materials

questions.answer: Important energy sources and structural materials

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: State two biological roles of lipids.
questions.answer: They can store energy, form cell membranes, provide insulation and participate in signaling; any two.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Why is a balanced diet important?
questions.answer: It supplies appropriate amounts of energy, essential nutrients, vitamins, minerals, water and fibre needed for growth, repair and healthy body function.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Compare carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids in terms of basic building units and major roles.
questions.answer: Award one mark for each biomolecule group plus one mark for a clear comparison linking structure/building units to function.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A polymer is made from many smaller units called?
questions.answer: Monomers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Addition polymerization commonly involves monomers containing?
questions.answer: Carbon-carbon double bonds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Give one natural polymer and one synthetic polymer.
questions.answer: Examples: cellulose or protein as natural; poly(ethene), nylon or PVC as synthetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Why can some synthetic polymers create environmental problems?
questions.answer: Many degrade very slowly, accumulate as waste and can fragment into persistent particles unless reduced, reused, recycled or managed responsibly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Explain monomers, polymerization, repeating units and responsible management of polymer materials.
questions.answer: Award marks for defining monomer/polymer, polymerization, repeating unit concept, useful material properties/applications, and waste/recycling considerations.
